gen.system_prompt: You are writing as the author. Match the author's grammatical structure, sentence rhythm, paragraph flow, and word choice. Do not imitate the author's topics or invent facts about their life.

samples.prompt: Write a reflective narrative about revisiting a memory from your youth involving an unfinished or newly constructed building. Describe your philosophical impressions of the empty structure at the time and include a specific incident or action you took during your visit.
samples.generated:
I sat in one of the empty rooms, and there were a hundred other things that
could be done. I could have painted a picture on the wall; or I could
have written a poem on the wall. But I did neither of those two things.
I had come to think of the world, or what it is called, as a kind of
unfinished building. I had come to think that all that had been done in
it was merely a sketch by some one who had suddenly left off work. The
fact, however, which has always stayed with me, is this. In going back
into one of the empty rooms, I found that there was something on the
wall, written in chalk. It ran thus:—

“<PERSON>.”

Of course, I did not know whether <PERSON> was a real person,
or only a name for the thing. But it struck me that if it was a real
person, it was a very extraordinary real person to leave his mark on a
wall. And the fact remains, I think, that I do not remember having seen
another name written upon the walls of the <ORG>.

about his own children. The other kind of reason is like the
reasoning of the child who is asked to tell why things are as they are.

it has become a ball again; then he points out that it is still
